title: Horizontal acceleration correct
description: Essential: Student correctly computes the acceleration on the horizontal plane using Newton's second law, accounting for applied force and kinetic friction.

title: Velocity at B correct
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the speed at point B using kinematics (e.g., v² = 2aL) with the proper horizontal acceleration and distance L.

title: Incline deceleration correct
description: Important: Student correctly determines the deceleration on the incline using forces, including both gravity and kinetic friction components.

title: Maximum distance correct
description: Essential: Student correctly computes the maximum distance up the incline using kinematics (e.g., 0 - v_B² = 2(-a₁)x) with the proper deceleration.

title: Force diagram reasoning
description: Important: Student's solution shows clear application of Newton's second law on both the horizontal and inclined segments, identifying all relevant forces.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student's work maintains consistent units (m, s, kg, N) and includes them in final answers.

title: Sign error in kinematics
description: Pitfall: Student uses an incorrect sign for acceleration on the incline in the kinematic equation for stopping distance.

title: Friction force mistake
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly calculates the friction force on the horizontal plane or on the incline (e.g., omitting the normal force component).
